subject: physics_2
question_text: Explain the distance of closest approach and impact parameter.

mark_split.label: Distance of closest approach — the definition
The relation between b and θ

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: at the distance of closest approach the whole kinetic energy of the α-particle has become electrostatic potential energy, ½mv² = (1/4πε₀)(2Ze²/r₀), so r₀ = (1/4πε₀)(2Ze²/Kα) with Kα = ½mv²; the factor 2 is the α-particle's own charge +2e. For the impact parameter, b = Ze² cot(θ/2)/[4πε₀(½mv²)].

recall_prompt: Define the distance of closest approach and derive r₀, then define the impact parameter and give its relation to θ.

steps.label: Distance of closest approach
lines: Distance of closest approach:
The minimum distance from the centre of a
nucleus that an α-particle can reach in a
head-on collision is called the distance of
closest approach, r₀.
As the α-particle comes near the positive
nucleus it is repelled, slows down, stops for a
moment at r₀ and then retraces its path, so it
is scattered through 180°.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say head-on, say it stops, say it retraces its path.
steps.why: Only a head-on approach defines r₀: any other path curves away before the particle reaches its nearest point on that straight line. At r₀ the speed is zero for an instant, which is what makes the energy equation simple.
common_mistakes: Saying the α-particle touches the nucleus. It stops before reaching it.
Confusing r₀ with the nuclear radius. r₀ is an upper limit on the nuclear size, not the size itself.

recall.must_convey: That r₀ is the minimum distance from the nucleus reached in a head-on collision, where the α-particle stops and retraces its path.
accept: minimum distance from the centre of the nucleus
it stops and retraces its path
reject: perpendicular distance of the velocity vector

steps.memory_tip: Straight at the nucleus, stop, come straight back — the turning point is r₀.

steps.label: The expression for r₀
lines: At r₀ the whole kinetic energy of the
α-particle has become electrostatic potential
energy of the α-particle and the nucleus:
A faster α-particle has a smaller r₀.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The 2 in 2Ze² is the α-particle's own charge +2e.
steps.why: Energy is conserved: kinetic energy far away equals potential energy at the turning point, where the speed is zero. The charges are +2e for the α-particle and +Ze for the nucleus, which is where 2Ze² comes from.
common_mistakes: Writing Ze² and losing the factor 2. The α-particle carries +2e.
Adding a kinetic term at r₀. The particle is momentarily at rest there.

accept: half m v squared equals two Z e squared by four pi epsilon nought r nought
r nought equals two Z e squared by four pi epsilon nought K alpha

steps.memory_tip: All the kinetic energy is spent at the turning point — set the two energies equal.

steps.label: Impact parameter
lines: Impact parameter:
The impact parameter of an α-particle is the
perpendicular distance of the velocity vector
of the α-particle from the centre of the
nucleus, measured when the α-particle is far
away from the atom. It is denoted by b.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Perpendicular distance, of the velocity vector, from the centre of the nucleus.
steps.why: b and r₀ are different distances: b is measured on the straight incoming line before the path bends, while r₀ is the nearest point actually reached. They are equal only in the sense that b = 0 gives the head-on case.
common_mistakes: Defining b as the distance of closest approach. That is r₀.
Leaving out "far away". Near the nucleus the path is already curved.

recall.must_convey: That b is the perpendicular distance of the α-particle's velocity vector from the centre of the nucleus, measured far away.
accept: perpendicular distance of the velocity vector
from the centre of the nucleus
measured when it is far away
reject: minimum distance reached in a head on collision

steps.memory_tip: b is measured on the straight line in; r₀ is measured on the way through.

steps.label: b and the angle θ
lines: Rutherford found the relation
1. Large b — small scattering angle θ, so the
deflection is small.
2. Small b — large scattering angle θ, so the
deflection is large.
3. b = 0 gives θ = 180°: the α-particle is
aimed at the centre and retraces its path.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The formula plus all three cases.
steps.why: cot(θ/2) falls steadily as θ rises from 0° to 180°, and cot(90°) = 0, so the formula itself contains the three cases — a large b gives a small turn, and b = 0 gives the full 180°.
common_mistakes: Giving only one of the three cases. The examiner marks the set.

recall.must_convey: That b = Ze² cot(θ/2)/[4πε₀(½mv²)], with large b giving small θ and b = 0 giving θ = 180°.
accept: Z e squared cot theta by two
b zero gives one eighty degrees

steps.memory_tip: cot(90°) = 0, so b = 0 sits exactly at θ = 180°.

insider_note: Two quantities are asked for, so the page needs two headings — r₀ with its energy equation, and b with its cot(θ/2) relation.
